items.title: The natural numbers together with the rationals are two-universal for countable linear orders
items.author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 809-812: the class consisting of the natural numbers and the rationals is two-universal for all countable linear orders, and in particular the rationals alone are two-universal for the infinite ones. The statement gives no witness and no rank bookkeeping, and the proof (source lines 813-818) has to supply both: it separates the finite orders, which are already members, from the infinite ones, for which the comparison at rank two has to be produced through a rank one comparison of intervals, using that every interval of the rationals is infinite while an interval of an arbitrary countable order need not be. The reduction of a rank two comparison to a single interval comparison is the whole argument and it is invisible in the statement.
